source.title: FinchGPT: a Transformer based language model for birdsong analysis
source.authors: Kosei Kobayashi; Kosuke Matsuzaki; Masaya Taniguchi; Keisuke Sakaguchi; Kentaro Inui; Kentaro Abe

record.file_problem: Whole paper text is present; no apparent truncation or corruption.
record.tranche_reason: The study varies model architecture and training-corpus size and measures held-out next-token cross-entropy in a new setting: textualized Bengalese finch songs. It does not reproduce or fit the original language-model scaling laws.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Kaplan et al. for scaling laws, then reports its own cross-entropy results while varying FinchGPT layer count, hidden dimension, and training-data size. It does not fit a power law, test extrapolation, vary compute, or find a compute-optimal allocation. Other findings, including attention-span restriction and HVC ablation, are not scaling-law results.
record.test_reason: The study trains GPT-2-style transformers from scratch on textualized Bengalese finch song. It varies layer count, hidden dimension and corpus size (about 10 to 10^3 kB per Fig 1H) and reports held-out next-token cross-entropy. That is a scaling result in a non-human-language setting, so it bears on V5. It fits no power law, has no compute axis, and does no extrapolation or allocation analysis.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is largely correct. The authors also conclude that loss gains per data doubling peak near 30 kB, so about 40 days of recording suffices for most birds. They make no claim about power-law form.
record.recipe_differences: Uses GPT-2-equivalent models trained on textualized birdsong; varies a limited set of architecture dimensions and corpus sizes. It does not reproduce the original human-language scaling-law fits, compute sweep, or extrapolation procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: Cross-entropy changed with layer count and corpus size, but not significantly with hidden-state dimension from 192 to 768. The loss-reduction rate for medium and large models when doubling data peaked around 30 kB.
record.problems: The study reports no power-law fits, exponents, compute sweep, compute-optimal allocation, or small-to-large extrapolation. The text gives qualitative outcomes rather than exact cross-entropy values for the scaling comparisons. The tested setting is a birdsong corpus, and the text does not state parameter counts for the compared configurations.
record.rows_left_out: No scaling-related results were left out. Other reported experiments, including attention-span restriction and HVC ablation, do not test the claim versions about scaling laws.

untested.parts: Human-text LM pretraining is not studied; all runs are on birdsong.
All of it; there is no compute budget or allocation analysis.
Shape is not compared at a fixed parameter count.
The power-law functional form, exponents, and range across several orders of magnitude in parameters or compute.
There are no fits, so fitting choices are not compared.

missing.what: The data-size range spans about two orders of magnitude (x-axis 10^1 to 10^3 kB). Cross-entropy runs from about 1.5 to about 0.5 and is readable only from the figure.

record.verdict_notes: The scaling section is a small side analysis in a birdsong-modelling paper. It cites Kaplan et al. but fits no law. The result reads as a loss curve that bends rather than a clean power law; this is qualitative only.

versions.untested_parts: Tests loss trends while varying layers, hidden dimensions, and corpus size in this setting; does not fit a power law, test several orders of magnitude, or vary compute.
No small-run fit is used to predict the loss of larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or compute-optimal parameter/token counts.
Architecture dimensions are varied, but not compared at a fixed parameter count.
Tests loss trends for textualized birdsong with model and corpus-size variation; does not establish the same power-law form, fit its exponents, or test other modalities or training regimes.
No downstream-task performance is related to scale or pretraining loss.
No comparison of fitting choices, fitted exponents, or curve bending.

rows.subject: FinchGPT
rows.size_stated: Layer sweep: 1L, 3L, 6L, and 12L; A = L, H = 192
rows.operation_detail: Varied layer count and measured next-token cross-entropy
rows.value: Cross-entropy decreased steadily as layer numbers increased; the 1L, 1A model was significantly worse.
rows.uncertainty: Mean ± SEM; n = 235,256 predictions across 2,660 songs (Fig. 1G caption).
rows.note: The text describes the trend but gives no cross-entropy values or fitted curve.
rows.check: Birdsong is a different modality, not human-text LM pretraining, so the link to V1 is removed. Loss falls steadily with layers (1 to 12), but no power-law form is fitted and the Fig 1G range is small (about 0.50 to 0.56). For a version naming the power-law form, this is partial.

rows.subject: FinchGPT
rows.operation_detail: Varied hidden-state dimension and measured next-token cross-entropy
rows.value: Increasing hidden states from 192 to 768 did not significantly affect cross-entropy.
rows.uncertainty: Mean ± SEM; n = 235,256 predictions across 2,660 songs (Fig. 1G caption).
rows.note: The text explicitly reports no significant cross-entropy effect across the tested hidden-state dimensions; parameter counts are not stated.
rows.check: The link to V1 is removed for the same modality reason. The text says hidden size 192 to 768 'did not significantly affect cross-entropy'. This was at a fixed 695 kB corpus, so data may be the bottleneck.

relationships.condition: FinchGPT on birdsong; layer sweep and data-size sweep, small, medium and large models
relationships.reason: Loss falls steadily with more layers and more data, and larger models are lower at all data sizes (r1, r3–r7). This is direction only: no power-law fit.
relationships.display_finding: Loss decreased steadily with more layers and data, and larger models achieved lower loss at every data size, without a power-law fit.

relationships.condition: Hidden dimension 192 to 768 at L=6, A=6, 695 kB corpus
relationships.reason: Widening the model gave no significant loss change (r2), so more parameters did not lower loss in this setting.
relationships.display_finding: Increasing hidden dimension from 192 to 768 produced no significant loss change.
